summary: AE and SE aligned with Cygnus on a 6-week POC focused on quality gating: golden prompts, regression checks, hallucination detection, format validation, and scoring rubric. Discussed workload sizing, latency vs cost tradeoffs, private deployment constraints (VPC/KMS), and benchmark plan. Next: SOW, benchmark harness, and delivery of golden/regression sets.
transcript:
[00:00] Olivia Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time today. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Dr. Lena Morales: Lena here, hi.
[00:08] Amit Verma: Amit on the line.
[00:10] Sara Klein: Sara here.
[00:12] Marcus Diaz: Marcus, Redwood SE.
[00:15] Priya Anand: Priya, CSM.
[00:18] Olivia Chen: Great. Goal for today is to align on POC scope — specifically the quality evaluation plan: golden prompts, regression sets, hallucination checks, scoring, and timeline. We'll also walk through a quick workload sizing ask.
[00:34] Dr. Lena Morales: Sounds good. To frame, our use case is clinical-trial document summarization and extraction. Accuracy and hallucination avoidance are absolute blockers for us.
[00:45] Sara Klein: Right, downstream QA needs deterministic formats for ingestion, so format checks are as important as free-text quality.
[00:52] Marcus Diaz: Understood — so two dimensions: content correctness and structural/format correctness. We'll propose separate gates.
[00:58] Olivia Chen: For success criteria, proposed: 1) pass rate on golden prompt set >= 90% (weighted by severity), 2) hallucination rate below 2% on a curated hallucination test, 3) format conformance 99% on schema checks. Thoughts?
[01:16] Dr. Lena Morales: 90% seems reasonable if severity weighting is clear. We want the ability to prioritize clinical fields — patient id, dosage, outcome flags.
[01:28] Amit Verma: Quick infra note: we probably need VPC + KMS; PII never leaves our VPC in prod. How does Redwood handle that in a pilot?
[01:37] Marcus Diaz: For pilots we can offer Private control plane or dedicated capacity. Private will keep your data within the VPC and we can connect via a peered subnet. KMS integration for key wrapping is supported. We'll scope that in the SOW.
[01:50] Sara Klein: Any SLA during the POC?
[01:53] Olivia Chen: POC has standard trial terms; we can provide target latency SLOs for the baseline runs but full SLA only on Dedicated. We'll capture expectations in the SOW.
[02:05] [02:05] Dr. Lena Morales: Ok. On the golden prompts: we're planning to provide ~500 curated prompts that represent core document types, plus 50 edge-case formats. Will that be enough for meaningful coverage?
[02:18] Marcus Diaz: 500 is a solid start. For statistical significance on pass rates, it's decent; we'll also ask for 200 regression examples that represent historical failure modes.
[02:28] Olivia Chen: We'll also recommend ~100 adversarial and hallucination-focused probes to stress-test. Marcus, do you want to cover how we'll score?
[02:36] Marcus Diaz: Sure. We'll run automated rubric checks first: field-level exact/regex matches for structured outputs; fuzzy scoring for free-text with heuristics like normalized BLEU and entity F1. Then human review on a sampled subset — about 5–10% of outputs — to calibrate the automatic thresholds. We'll produce a combined score: 70% auto metrics + 30% human calibration to avoid metric gaming.
[02:56] Sara Klein: How do you detect hallucinations automatically?
[02:59] Marcus Diaz: A combination: 1) NER-based factuality checks against source doc, 2) provenance heuristics (does the model quote or invent?), 3) model confidence signals and token-level surprise. It's imperfect; that's why we add the human sample.
[03:12] [03:12] Dr. Lena Morales: Can you flag hallucinations by severity? Some extraneous synonyms are low severity but inventing a dosage is high severity.
[03:20] Marcus Diaz: Yep — severity buckets: cosmetic, incorrect-but-noncritical, and critical. We'll weight the scoring so critical errors fail the prompt regardless of other passes.
[03:30] Olivia Chen: On workload sizing — you're planning about 20k docs/month, average doc length 1.2k tokens, peak QPS around 8. Is that still accurate?
[03:41] Amit Verma: Yes, but we have ingestion bursts during nightly ETL windows up to 60 QPS for ~15 minutes.
[03:48] Marcus Diaz: For bursts, we can set up burst capacity on Dedicated or use Redwood's autoscaling with queueing tolerance. But that affects per-token cost vs latency. For the POC we'll simulate both steady-state and burst scenarios in the benchmark.
[04:00] Sara Klein: Cost is a big concern. How will Redwood help estimate unit economics?
[04:04] Olivia Chen: We'll run baseline token counts with typical prompts and produce an estimated cost per document under hosted vs dedicated vs quantized private model runs, and include suggestions: batching, prefix caching, quantization.
[04:14] Dr. Lena Morales: For the benchmark specifics — can we agree on three buckets? 1) golden set pass rate, 2) regression pass rate and triage report, 3) performance: p99 latency and cost per 1k docs.
[04:28] Marcus Diaz: Yes. And we'll add hallucination severity breakdown and format-conformance percentage. For latency we'll capture p50/p95/p99 under both 8 QPS steady and 60 QPS burst.
[04:40] Olivia Chen: Timeline proposal: week 0 — finalize SOW and dataset handoff; week 1 — Redwood baseline run + harness; week 2–3 — iterative tuning and quantization experiments; week 4 — locked benchmark run; week 5 — human calibration and results review; week 6 — executive review and acceptance. That's six weeks.
[05:00] Dr. Lena Morales: That aligns with our internal timeline, but we may need exec review earlier if results warrant.
[05:06] Sara Klein: Is there an expectation for what constitutes an accept vs reject at the executive level?
[05:09] Olivia Chen: We'll propose acceptance thresholds in the SOW: golden pass >= 90% (critical fields 98%), hallucination critical < 1%, format conformance >= 99%. Those are negotiable.
[05:20] Amit Verma: From a security perspective, we need SOC2-type controls and audit logs for any inference that touches PHI. Can Redwood provide audit trails during the pilot?
[05:28] Marcus Diaz: Yes, we can enable request-level audit logs and provide limited retention. For production-grade retention and encryption key control you'll want Private or Dedicated with KMS/HSM options.
[05:38] [05:38] Dr. Lena Morales: For human review, can we bring our clinical SMEs or will Redwood provide annotators?
[05:43] Priya Anand: Typically customers bring domain SMEs; Redwood can support with annotation tooling and recommended sampling rules. We can also provide managed labeling as an add-on if needed.
[05:54] Sara Klein: How will you handle inter-annotator variance?
[05:57] Marcus Diaz: We'll use calibration sessions and compute Cohen's kappa on a seed set to measure agreement. If variance is high, we tighten rubric or increase sample size.
[06:09] Olivia Chen: Ok let's capture the deliverables: SOW + acceptance criteria doc, benchmark harness & runbook, baseline results, tuning notes, human calibration results, final acceptance report.
[06:21] Dr. Lena Morales: Agreed. A couple of small questions — do you support model pinning across rollouts? We can't have changing model behavior mid-eval.
[06:29] Marcus Diaz: Yes, we pin model versions and snapshot model binaries for the locked benchmark. Redwood supports model variant fallback but for accepted runs we'll freeze the model and config.
[06:40] Sara Klein: About scoring — can we get a sample rubric?
[06:43] Marcus Diaz: We'll send a sample matrix: field-level exact, field-level fuzzy with thresholds, hallucination flags, overall pass/fail logic.
[06:51] Amit Verma: On the integration side — what's the sample throughput for a single GPU in Redwood Dedicated for 1.2k token docs?
[06:58] Marcus Diaz: Roughly 60–80 tokens/sec per GPU depending on model and quantization; with batching you can get equivalent higher throughput. We'll include concrete numbers in the baseline.
[07:09] [07:09] Dr. Lena Morales: If the baseline fails our critical fields, what's the typical remediation path?
[07:14] Olivia Chen: We iterate: prompt tuning, system prompt engineering, model spec changes (larger or specialized model), and quantization adjustments. For significant regressions we can propose an extended tuning phase.
[07:25] Sara Klein: Any regulatory issues with storing golden prompts in Redwood? We prefer them encrypted at rest.
[07:32] Marcus Diaz: All customer data in Private or Dedicated is encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys if desired. We'll note that in the SOW.
[07:40] Dr. Lena Morales: Good. Are there any benchmarks you recommend we run for hallucination specifically?
[07:45] Marcus Diaz: We'll run targeted probes that remove the answer from the source text, force extrapolation, and create paraphrase contexts. We'll also run provenance checks comparing model outputs back to source spans.
[07:57] Olivia Chen: Anything else from the Cygnus side?
[08:00] Sara Klein: No, I think we've covered most. We'll send the golden and regression sets by next Thursday.
[08:06] Amit Verma: I'll send the VPC diagram and constraints.
[08:09] Dr. Lena Morales: Looking forward to the SOW.
[08:12] Olivia Chen: Great — recap of next steps: I send SOW; Marcus provides harness; customer sends datasets; schedule deep-dive. We will follow up with calendar invites.
[08:23] [08:23] End of recording

Notes: transcription contains occasional speaker overlap and mis-attributed short segments (autogenerated). Some technical terms transcribed with slight variants (e.g., K V cache, S A M L references). Intent preserved.
